Receipts (£bn)!C43.raw: A full list of sources is available in the glossary.

Glossary!C5.raw: Revenue relating to activities in the current year, comprising mainly direct and indirect taxes, but also including social security contributions, interest, dividends, capital taxes and profits from trading activities.

Glossary!C11.raw: The difference between total public sector receipts and expenditure on an accrued basis each year. As the widest measure of borrowing it is a key indicator of the fiscal position. PSNB is the headline measure of 'the deficit'.

Glossary!C14.raw: A stock measure of the public sector's net liability position i.e. its liabilities minus its liquid assets. It is broadly the stock equivalent of public sector net borrowing, but measured on a cash rather than an accrued basis. It is also the fiscal measure used for the Government's supplementary fiscal target. PSND is the key measure of the country's overall debt.

Glossary!C15.raw: A measure of the amount of cash which is needed to make up the difference betweeen spending and revenues. This is different from net borrowing as it also includes financial transactions, which will affect the cash position but are not included in net borrowing. Public sector net debt is driven by changes in the public sector net cash requirement.

Contents!D4.raw:
This database contains receipts, spending and fiscal aggregates back to 1700. These are not national statistics and judgements have been made in places to ensure consistency in the figures across years. A full list of notes and sources is provided at the bottom. 


Choose a chart from the dropdown menu:

Contents!D31.raw: All data, unless otherwise stated, are on a March-ending financial year basis. For non March-ending financial years, figures are linearly interpolated.

Contents!D34.raw: Unless otherwise stated, figures are from the Bank of England millennium dataset until 1948-49 and ONS thereafter. ONS figures are consistent with the 23 May Public Sector Finances release.

Contents!D35.raw: Receipts are on a cash basis until 1998-99 and accruals basis thereafter.

Contents!D36.raw: 1Income tax, NICs, Capital Gains Tax and Windfall tax receipts sourced from Bank of England millennium dataset until 1998-99. National insurance contributions are consistent with social security contributions from Middleton (1996) until 1946-47.

Contents!D37.raw: 2Corporation tax series is consistent with ONS series N445 prior to 1999-00 and CPRN thereafter.

Contents!D38.raw: 3Petroleum revenue tax, petroleum royalties, gas levy are consistent with table 11.11 from ONS 'Statistics of government revenues from UK oil and gas production' (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/government-revenues-from-uk-oil-and-gas-production--2)

Contents!D39.raw: 4VAT receipts are inclusive of refunds to central and local government bodies.

Contents!D40.raw: 5Prior to 1999-00, custom and excise duties are consistent with ONS series NMYB less GTBC

Contents!D41.raw: 6Other central government receipts includes smaller receipts lines, as well as central government interest and dividends and gross operating surplus.

Contents!D42.raw: 7An adjustment has been made to central government receipts in 1919-20 and 1920-21 to ensure consistency with total public sector receipts.

Contents!D43.raw: 8Other public sector receipts includes smaller non-central government receipts, as well as non-central government interest and dividends and gross operating surplus.

Contents!D62.raw: 1 PSNB sourced from Bank of England (2017) from 1700-01 to 1899-00, then from OBR (2023) for 1900-01 onwards. Due to availability of data, from 1700-01 to 1899-00 our PSNB series is showing Central Government Net Borrowing.

Contents!D63.raw: 2 PSND sourced from Bank of England (2017) from 1700-01 to 1899-00, then from OBR (2023) for 1900-01 onwards.

3 Note on coverage of the nominal GDP series which follows the political boundaries in place at any given time:
- From 1700-01 to 1800-01, Great Britain GDP (England, Wales and Scotland) – this is a simplification of the historical political boundaries as the Exchequer only started imposing taxes on Scotland post the commencement of the Acts of Union on 1 May 1707. 
- From 1800-01 to 1921-22, GB and Irish (both North and South) GDP, receipts and spending from the Exchequer covered the whole of the UK and Ireland’s geography at that time. 
- From 1922-23 onwards GB and Northern Irish GDP as Anglo-Irish Treaty came fully into effect on 31 March 1922.

Contents!D4.raw:
This database contains receipts, spending and fiscal aggregates back to 1700. These are not national statistics and judgements have been made in places to ensure consistency in the figures across years. A full list of notes and sources is provided at the bottom. 


Choose a chart from the dropdown menu:

Contents!D31.raw: All data, unless otherwise stated, are on a March-ending financial year basis. For non March-ending financial years, figures are linearly interpolated.

Contents!D34.raw: Unless otherwise stated, figures are from the Bank of England millennium dataset until 1948-49 and ONS thereafter. ONS figures are consistent with the 23 May Public Sector Finances release.

Contents!D35.raw: Receipts are on a cash basis until 1998-99 and accruals basis thereafter.

Contents!D36.raw: 1Income tax, NICs, Capital Gains Tax and Windfall tax receipts sourced from Bank of England millennium dataset until 1998-99. National insurance contributions are consistent with social security contributions from Middleton (1996) until 1946-47.

Contents!D37.raw: 2Corporation tax series is consistent with ONS series N445 prior to 1999-00 and CPRN thereafter.

Contents!D38.raw: 3Petroleum revenue tax, petroleum royalties, gas levy are consistent with table 11.11 from ONS 'Statistics of government revenues from UK oil and gas production' (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/government-revenues-from-uk-oil-and-gas-production--2)

Contents!D39.raw: 4VAT receipts are inclusive of refunds to central and local government bodies.

Contents!D40.raw: 5Prior to 1999-00, custom and excise duties are consistent with ONS series NMYB less GTBC

Contents!D41.raw: 6Other central government receipts includes smaller receipts lines, as well as central government interest and dividends and gross operating surplus.

Contents!D42.raw: 7An adjustment has been made to central government receipts in 1919-20 and 1920-21 to ensure consistency with total public sector receipts.

Contents!D43.raw: 8Other public sector receipts includes smaller non-central government receipts, as well as non-central government interest and dividends and gross operating surplus.

Contents!D62.raw: 1 PSNB sourced from Bank of England (2017) from 1700-01 to 1899-00, then from OBR (2023) for 1900-01 onwards. Due to availability of data, from 1700-01 to 1899-00 our PSNB series is showing Central Government Net Borrowing.

Contents!D63.raw: 2 PSND sourced from Bank of England (2017) from 1700-01 to 1899-00, then from OBR (2023) for 1900-01 onwards.

Contents!D64.raw:
3 Note on coverage of the nominal GDP series which follows the political boundaries in place at any given time:
- From 1700-01 to 1800-01, Great Britain GDP (England, Wales and Scotland) – this is a simplification of the historical political boundaries as the Exchequer only started imposing taxes on Scotland post the commencement of the Acts of Union on 1 May 1707. 
- From 1800-01 to 1921-22, GB and Irish (both North and South) GDP, receipts and spending from the Exchequer covered the whole of the UK and Ireland’s geography at that time. 
- From 1922-23 onwards GB and Northern Irish GDP as Anglo-Irish Treaty came fully into effect on 31 March 1922.

Glossary!C14.raw: A stock measure of the public sector's net liability position i.e. its liabilities minus its liquid assets. Glossary!C15.raw: A measure of the amount of cash which is needed to make up the difference betweeen spending and revenues. Public sector net debt is driven by changes in the public sector net cash requirement.

limitations: Receipts are not all tax. Non-tax is the difference between PSCR and National Accounts taxes, not the mixed residual column.
Other taxes are an explicit residual after named taxes; retained notes do not separately establish refund classification within National Accounts taxes.
Historical receipts are cash through 1998-99 and accruals thereafter; do not splice vintages or compare across this break without a bridge.
Historical central-government components can overlap licence fees before 1999-00 despite the U6 derivation; unresolved differences are retained, not assigned a rounding tolerance.
In the October 2026 databank debt is a cash stock at end March, borrowing an annual accrual flow. Changes in debt need not equal borrowing.
Debt shares use March-centred GDP; separately sourced published shares need not reproduce currency-unit stock ratios exactly. No discrepancy error bound is established.
Historical actual/estimate status is uncertain. May 2023 series are not October 2026 forecasts; no next release date is established here.
Historical borrowing uses a central-government proxy before 1900-01; the retained notes do not establish its accounting basis, so historical borrowing basis remains uncertain.

Historical debt remains a stock with uncertain accounting basis and scope in both source regimes: Bank of England (2017) through 1899-00 and OBR (2023) from 1900-01, as named in Contents!D63. The October 2026 glossary is not evidence for this historical series.
The historical geography note overlaps at 1800-01; that year is marked uncertain rather than choosing one boundary.
